scope: Targeted primary-source review; not a systematic review or exhaustive prior-art search
selection: Relevant original evidence on reader response, novelty, motivation, canonicity, cultural diffusion and measured game retention; plus three bounded classic-text examples.
excluded_from_evidence: Secondary summaries used only for discovery
Heo and Park game satiation paper, discovered but not included in this register
Unverified metadata crawl dates as publication dates

sources.title: Why Read the Classics?
sources.finding: Rereading can encounter changed readers and renewed discovery.
sources.limit: An author's interpretive proposal; no causal measurement of canon formation.

sources.title: Art as Technique
sources.access: primary essay in English translation, university-hosted PDF; targeted passages
sources.finding: Defamiliarization interrupts automatic recognition and redirects perception.
sources.limit: Theory, not a retention experiment. Hosted translation attribution/date not verified.

sources.authors: Peter Dixon; Marisa Bortolussi; Leslie C. Twilley; Alice Leung
sources.title: Literary processing and interpretation: Towards empirical foundations
sources.access: primary university-hosted PDF; targeted methods/results, including local PDF extraction
sources.finding: Two reading experiments distinguish text features from reader effects; appreciation changes depend on story and reader group.
sources.limit: Immediate prompted rereading; limited texts/populations; not voluntary return or historical endurance.

sources.title: Foregrounding, defamiliarization, and affect: Response to literary stories
sources.access: authors' university publication page reproducing primary abstract; publisher abstract indexed
sources.finding: Four studies associate foregrounded segments with longer reading, strikingness and affect.
sources.limit: Segment effects do not demonstrate long-term liking, voluntary rereading or canon survival.

sources.title: What Is Interesting? Exploring the Appraisal Structure of Interest
sources.access: primary paper abstract indexed on PubMed; UNCG repository PDF indexed but direct fetch timed out
sources.finding: Four experiments support novelty-complexity and coping-potential appraisals in interest.
sources.limit: Short-term interest; neither a universal optimum nor longitudinal game retention.

sources.title: Exploration of Novelty as Part of the Player Experience of Need Satisfaction in Games
sources.access: primary publisher abstract indexed; direct open failed CDN redirect
sources.finding: Survey of 390 online game players: novelty uniquely associates with concentration, satisfaction and commitment.
sources.limit: Cross-sectional self-report; no randomized novelty intervention or observed return duration. Online 15 March 2024; issue assignment 38(3), May 2026.

sources.authors: Richard M. Ryan; C. Scott Rigby; Andrew Przybylski
sources.title: The Motivational Pull of Video Games: A Self-Determination Theory Approach
sources.access: primary university-hosted PDF; abstract and targeted methods/results across four studies
sources.finding: Need satisfaction relates to enjoyment and future-play preference; Study 1 also measured immediate continuation choice.
sources.limit: Immediate choice differs from future intention. Not a months-long novelty manipulation.

sources.authors: Jonathan D. Leavitt; Nicholas J. S. Christenfeld
sources.title: The fluency of spoilers: Why giving away endings improves stories
sources.access: primary publisher abstract; paywalled full text not reviewed
sources.finding: Three experiments report spoiler benefits with fluency and story/spoiler qualifications.
sources.limit: Effects depend on materials and conditions; cannot generalize to every narrative or gameplay challenge.

sources.authors: Benjamin K. Johnson; Judith E. Rosenbaum
sources.title: Spoiler alert: Consequences of narrative spoilers for dimensions of enjoyment, appreciation, and transportation
sources.access: primary university author record reproducing abstract
sources.finding: Within-subject experiment, N=412, favored unspoiled stories on several enjoyment dimensions.
sources.limit: Conflicts with a blanket spoiler-benefit claim; abstract-only review cannot resolve every design difference.

sources.authors: Jean Barré; Thierry Poibeau; Jean-Baptiste Camps
sources.title: Operationalizing Canonicity: A Quantitative Study of French 19th and 20th Century Literature
sources.access: primary publisher full HTML; targeted framing, criteria and limitations
sources.finding: Operationalizes contemporary French reception, emphasizing schools; models textual associations with canonicity.
sources.limit: Contemporary classification, not causal proof of centuries of endurance. Current publisher citation gives 8(3); author preprint lists 8(1).

sources.authors: Kunwoo Park; Meeyoung Cha; Haewoon Kwak; Kuan-Ta Chen
sources.title: Achievement and Friends: Key Factors of Player Retention Vary Across Player Levels in Online Multiplayer Games
sources.access: primary author preprint abstract on arXiv
sources.finding: Logs for 51,104 players: achievement/social predictors vary by player level.
sources.limit: Single online multiplayer setting; observational prediction does not isolate novelty or transfer directly to solo autoplay.

sources.authors: Markus Viljanen; Antti Airola; Jukka Heikkonen; Tapio Pahikkala
sources.title: Playtime Measurement with Survival Analysis
sources.access: primary author preprint PDF; targeted duration/censoring sections
sources.finding: Separates playtime measures and explains censoring and survival/hazard comparisons.
sources.limit: A measurement framework, not an estimated novelty effect; definitive churn is generally unobservable.

sources.authors: Matthew J. Salganik; Peter Sheridan Dodds; Duncan J. Watts
sources.title: Experimental Study of Inequality and Unpredictability in an Artificial Cultural Market
sources.access: primary author university-hosted paper and supplement; targeted design/results
sources.finding: Artificial music market, 14,341 participants: social information increased inequality and unpredictability.
sources.limit: Downloads in an experimental market; not century-scale canonization or game retention.

sources.title: How adoption speed affects the abandonment of cultural tastes
sources.access: primary full paper indexed; targeted abstract/discussion; direct open encountered CAPTCHA
sources.finding: French/US name histories and expecting-parent evidence relate rapid adoption to abandonment.
sources.limit: Adoption velocity is not novelty. Names are a cross-domain warning, not an effect estimate for games or novels.

sources.title: Pride and Prejudice
sources.access: Project Gutenberg edition with Saintsbury preface; targeted novel chapters I and XXXVI
sources.finding: Opening and Elizabeth's reassessment support an authored example of changing interpretation.
sources.limit: Chosen passages do not establish the cause of the novel's canonical status. Preface is distinct from Austen's text.

sources.title: Frankenstein; or, the modern Prometheus
sources.access: Project Gutenberg text; targeted chapter 10; full edition history not resolved
sources.finding: Creator and creature present conflicting perspectives and claims of responsibility.
sources.limit: 1818 is first publication, not a certified date/version of this digital text; character testimony is not author-endorsed fact.

sources.title: Candide
sources.access: Project Gutenberg English translation; targeted chapters IV–V and XXX
sources.finding: Pangloss's explanations conflict with suffering; ending turns toward practical work.
sources.limit: 1759 is original publication; translation specifics not used for linguistic claims. No evidence here for why the work endures.
